stories.notes: AC is empty and spec is null for a complex multi-platform CMS Live Preview feature. openspec must elaborate requirements and technical approach first; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Title rewritten to describe the concrete delivered behavior — rendering Contentstack draft entries via preview token — rather than the generic feature label. StoryKind is novel: this capability does not yet exist in the codebase. Attachment points are useContent (236 callers, central content path), ContentstackContext (provides CS config to the tree), services/contentstack.ts (API layer that must forward preview params), and pages/[[...slug]].tsx (page router that must enter preview mode). VCs derived from description since ACs are empty.

Openspec produced zero acceptance criteria, so I authored the full set from the story title ('Render Contentstack draft entries via preview token for CMS live preview'), description ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), and the listed attachment-point files. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core happy-path and no-regression baseline; (2) AC-3/AC-4 cover error and edge-case paths for invalid tokens and API failures; (3) AC-5 ensures draft data propagates through the component tree, not just the top-level page; (4) AC-6 is a security criterion — preview tokens and API keys must not leak to the client bundle; (5) AC-7 ensures preview mode can be exited; (6) AC-8 enforces cross-site (GO/UP/MX) parity; (7) AC-9 addresses the 'live preview' real-time update behavior implied by 'CMS live preview'; (8) AC-10 guards against performance regression on published paths; (9) AC-11 ensures tokens are not blindly trusted; (10) AC-12 adds an accessibility/UX safeguard — draft pages must be visually distinguishable from published ones. CAVEAT: File contents were not available for review, so assumptions about the current architecture (e.g., server-side token handling, cookie-based preview mode, real-time event bridge) may need refinement once the code is inspected. If Contentstack live preview does not use a real-time event model in this integration, AC-9 may be inapplicable and should be removed.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline division of labor broke down. Openspec identified attachment points and story kind (novel) but produced zero acceptance criteria despite ACs being empty — it failed its primary elaboration duty. Speckit compensated by authoring all 12 ACs from scratch, which is outside its review/harden role, and did so without inspecting file contents — meaning several ACs (notably AC-9 real-time event model) rest on unverified architectural assumptions. Both agents report acceptanceChanged:false despite speckit clearly authoring ACs, an inconsistency that undermines traceability. Speckit's AC design (security, error paths, cross-site parity, accessibility) shows good intent but cannot be trusted as hardened without code inspection. Human review needed to validate assumptions, reconcile the acceptanceChanged inconsistency, and determine whether AC-9 is applicable.
